model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Conaway: a D+5 seat, incumbency, a favorable national environment for Democrats, and a lopsided money edge over a poorly funded challenger. Markets agree, pricing the Democrat near 94%, so the race stays in Safe D territory.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or significant outside spending against Conaway would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Herb Conaway, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a New Jersey district that leans Democratic by about five points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, having raised over $930,000 and holding $439,000 on hand, while Republican Michael McGuire has raised under $80,000 and reports only about $800 in cash. Minor-party candidates are on the ballot but show no measurable support or funding.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on district lean, incumbency, fundraising, and prediction markets, all of which favor Conaway heavily. Markets price his win probability around 94 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the usual caveat that thin data leaves somewhat wider uncertainty than a well-polled contest.
